explanation.text:
Neginah--or, Neginoth (see on Psa 4:1, title). Separated from his usual spiritual privileges, perhaps by Absalom's rebellion, the Psalmist prays for divine aid, and, in view of past mercies, with great confidence of being heard. (Psa 61:1-8)

From the end--that is, places remote from the sanctuary (Deu 28:64).

bsb.title: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. Of David.
bsb.text: Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer.

explanation.text:
heart is overwhelmed--literally, "covered over with darkness," or, "distress."

to the rock-- (Psa 18:2; Psa 40:2).

higher than I--which otherwise I cannot ascend.

bsb.text: From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.

explanation.text: shelter . . . and strong tower--repeat the same sentiment.

bsb.text: For You have been my refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy.

explanation.text:
I will abide--So I desire to do (compare Psa 23:6).

trust in the covert, etc.--make my refuge, in the shadow (compare Psa 17:8; Psa 36:7).

bsb.text: Let me dwell in Your tent forever and take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah

explanation.text:
the heritage--or, part in the spiritual blessings of Israel (Psa 21:2-4).

vows--implies prayers.

bsb.text: For You have heard my vows, O God; You have given me the inheritance reserved for those who fear Your name.

explanation.text: the king--himself and his royal line ending in Christ. Mercy and truth personified, as in Psa 40:11; Psa 57:3.

bsb.text: Increase the days of the king’s life; may his years span many generations.

explanation.text: abide before God--literally, "sit as a king in God's presence," under His protection.

bsb.text: May he sit enthroned in God’s presence forever; appoint Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness to guard him.

explanation.text:
Thus for new blessings will new vows of praise ever be paid.

Next: Psalms Chapter 62

bsb.text: Then I will ever sing praise to Your name and fulfill my vows day by day.
